name: MKI Seerr Bridge
overview: Seerr inside Jellyfin: button, embedded view, search and sign-in.
description: Brings Seerr into the Jellyfin web client: a button in the header and side menu, Seerr embedded in Jellyfin instead of a redirect, Seerr suggestions under Jellyfin search results with one-click requests attributed to the right user, optional single sign-on via Quick Connect, and a compatibility bridge for clients that still send legacy X-Emby authorization headers.
changelog: Security update. Requests from the search results are made in the user's own Seerr account, matched by Jellyfin user ID, and are refused for accounts not linked to Seerr yet instead of running as the administrator; each user can send up to 30 per hour. Single sign-on can no longer be triggered by other websites, and the Seerr session cookie is set HttpOnly (and Secure over https). The settings endpoint needs a signed-in user, the plugin repository answers only inside the local network, the legacy header bridge only passes a single well-formed token, and calls to Seerr no longer follow redirects or keep cookies.
